title: Coefficient biduality map is compatible with shifts and triangles
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, small in the chosen universe, with a sheaf of commutative rings, and write $\mathcal D=D(\mathcal O)$ for its unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the derived internal Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and put $V^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(V,\mathcal O[0])$. Let $d_V:V\to V^{\vee\vee}$ be the transpose of coefficient evaluation after interchanging the tensor factors by Koszul symmetry [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. Then the natural transformation $d:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\to(-)^{\vee\vee}$ commutes with the signed shift comparisons for derived internal Hom, and for every distinguished triangle $V\to W\to Z\to V[1]$ its three components give a morphism to the triangle obtained by applying $(-)^{\vee\vee}$, including the square on the connecting map. Slice restriction to the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O|_U)$ of an object $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] carries this morphism of triangles to the corresponding one on the slice. Moreover let $R$ be a commutative ring acting centrally on $\mathcal O$, let $s\in R$, and let $\mathcal T\subset\mathcal D$ be a full $R$-linear triangulated subcategory preserved by $(-)^\vee$, with $R$-linear shifts. The transformation and these compatibilities descend to the raw scalar localization $\mathcal T[1/s]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Thus, both in $\mathcal D$ and in $\mathcal T[1/s]$, the class of objects with invertible $d_V$ is closed under shifts and two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles. No claim that an arbitrary $d_V$ is invertible is made.

proof.text: Apply normalized exactness of contravariant Hom at the coefficient unit. Compose its opposite with the double-opposite equivalence to obtain exactness of dual.rightOp, then compose with dual. Expand the opposite-functor and composite shift comparisons. The source normalizations at 1 and -1 show the degree-one composite is exactly signedShift, including its leading minus. This categorical derivation is the proved private signed_bidual_exact.

The separate degree-one evaluation lemma gives CommShiftCore for evaluation at 1. The proved generic commShiftCore_neg obtains compatibility at -n from n by applying shift n, zero and addition coherence, naturality and cancellation of isomorphisms. Integer induction with CommShiftCore.add then proves NatTrans.CommShift for every integer. Apply the already-proved triangleCompatibility_of: all three triangle squares, shift closure and every two-out-of-three implication follow. This is the complete Lean proof of ambient compatibility from two strictly smaller source results.

Apply ringedSiteSignedDual_restriction to the two supplied normalized closed models. This gives the actual fixed restriction functor F, its tensor and Hom comparisons t,h, the coefficient isomorphism o, evaluation and symmetry squares, and the normalized single-dual source-shift square. No replacement of F by an unspecified localization is used.

Prove preservation of the evaluation-defined bidual by transposing the evaluation restriction square. Naturality of the closed adjunction identifies transposes after restriction. Insert the symmetry square before transposition, and transport the coefficient object along o. The resulting composite is exactly the three factors in restrictionBidualIso. These arguments are the proved generic transpose_restriction, bidual_restriction_untransported, bidual_coefficient and bidual_restriction helpers. Only isomorphisms and transpose equivalences are canceled; no evaluation or biduality map is inverted.

Use normalized contravariant single-Hom exactness on both sites. Let alpha be the single-dual restriction isomorphism. Its degree-one shift square is precisely the source n=-1 formula above, after substituting the normalized single-Hom shifts, the opposite restriction shift, and their leading minus signs. CommShiftCore propagation proves alpha is shift-compatible. Apply rightOp, compose with alpha, and insert associators to form the double-dual natural isomorphism beta. Naturality and product functoriality identify beta pointwise with restrictionBidualIso. Expand the opposite and composite shift comparisons: the normalizations at 1 and -1 give exactly signedShift. The supplied bidual shift structures agree in degree one, so the proved generic integer propagation gives the required CommShift structure on beta for those supplied structures.

For a triangle V, use beta naturality at its connecting arrow and beta shift compatibility at V.obj1. Substitute the already established evaluation restriction square at V.obj3. Reassociating yields exactly the displayed restriction connecting-map equation. This identity holds for every triangle; the distinguished-triangle hypothesis is consequently not needed in this final calculation. Exactness of F separately preserves distinguished triangles.

The closed tensor–Hom adjunction makes tensoring additive: tensorRight is a left adjoint and hence preserves finite coproducts, and symmetry transfers additivity to tensorLeft. The central unit-action formula for a scalar identity, together with associator and right-unitor coherence, makes tensorLeft linear; symmetry gives the same for tensorRight. Transpose the source-naturality equation for evaluation. Since both tensor variables are additive and linear, the contravariant internal-Hom functor preserves sums and scalar multiplication. Apply this twice to obtain additivity and linearity of the actual bidual, then use injectivity of underlying full-subcategory morphisms to obtain subcategory_linearity. This is a direct closed-category argument, so no localization-fraction calculation is needed in this step.

proof.text: The ambient signed compatibility constructed in Steps 1–2 restricts to the full dual-stable triangulated subcategory: use the full inclusion to lift its coherent shift comparisons, and test exactness and the evaluation shift equation after that faithful inclusion. For scalar descent, compare the raw tensor-Hom category with the existing rationalization by the tensorHomEquiv linear equivalences. Tensor induction verifies its functor laws; these equivalences make the comparison fully faithful, and every rationalized object has a lattice, so it is an equivalence. Thus the raw Q is a categorical localization. The identity-component isomorphism Q composed with the extended F is isomorphic to F composed with Q. Mathlib localization descent gives a coherent CommShift structure on the extended F for all integer shifts, with the displayed Q comparison equation. Descend the natural transformation by the same universal property; its component is exactly Q(d_X). The unitor-adjusted whiskering equation proves shift compatibility after Q, and essential surjectivity on objects proves it before Q. Every localized distinguished triangle is isomorphic to a Q-image triangle; compare the two composite image-triangle functors to deduce exactness of the descended F. Apply the generic shift-compatible transformation triangle morphism construction to obtain all three squares. This argument works for the specified localization shift structure without using the extra degree-one hshift or hQ normalizations.

source.place: Scalar-localization construction and its specified distinguished triangles; blueprint lem-coef-rational-retract-evaluation, proof paragraph 3 (extension of the canonical comparisons).

proof.text: For any exact endofunctor F with a shift-compatible natural transformation d from the identity, use the canonical identity image-triangle isomorphism followed by NatTrans.mapTriangle to obtain the triangle map with components d. Mathlib triangle two-out-of-three for natural transformations gives all three invertibility implications. The formula for d on X[n] expresses it as the shifted d_X conjugated by the two shift comparisons, so invertibility of d_X implies invertibility of d_(X[n]). Conversely the shift equation gives invertibility of the shifted d_X, and the shift equivalence reflects isomorphisms. Apply this categorical argument both on the full subcategory and on its scalar localization in Step 8. The same categorical conclusion is available to the ambient signed construction in Steps 1–2; the ambient construction is reduced to the two separate source results above. The slice construction is assembled from the single-Hom source-shift comparison and generic closed-category transport in Steps 3–6.
